assumptions: Cases use synthetic Search Console and PostHog responses for northpine.example, served by step ID; tests/test_traffic_snapshot.py supplies them offline. They are not live evidence.
The ordinary case has a full year of daily Search Console rows, complete page and query reads, and complete PostHog landing, referrer, signup and reading reads.
The readout sits in the same file as the data, under readout.markdown, because a code workflow writes one artifact.
PostHog is optional. Every case here runs with it connected; the search-only run without it is covered offline in tests/test_traffic_snapshot.py, since a case cannot set a connection's state.
cost_drivers: No model calls and no Tin credits. At most four Search Console reads, each capped at 256000 bytes, and four PostHog reads capped at 64000 bytes; provider quotas and latency are unmeasured.
effects: Replaces analytics/traffic-snapshot.json in the project when at least one provider read returned data. No send, post, spend, edit or provider change.

cases.description: Pages, named and hidden clicks, sessions by channel, first-touch signups, team exclusions and a readout with a ChatGPT row.

contains: Direct is a measurement gap, not a channel

cases.description: A capped prior page read must not turn an unobserved prior page into zero or a new page.
A signup event PostHog never saw stays null and names the instrumentation gap.
Few sessions, no signup event and no project files; min_count 100, so nothing is called a change.
118 PostHog signups this week, 9 of them from paid sessions. The wrong result adds ad-platform conversions to site signups.

rubric.question: Do windows, channel counts, hidden clicks, nulls and prior values match the provider rows without filling in missing numbers?
Do session counts match PostHog's own session count for the same hosts, window and exclusions within one percent?
Does every PostHog read carry the host scope and the team exclusions, and does a failed read leave its fields unmeasured?
Are readout changes called only above min_count with the exact binomial test and Holm correction, and is Direct reported as a measurement gap?
Does each readout decision rest on a rule that fired, with its evidence and the workflow that acts on it?
